finding.claim: HIGH: The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation and returns the response body to the caller. An unauthenticated attacker can reach loopback, RFC-1918 hosts and cloud metadata such as http://169.254.169.254/ and read the responses. Go's default client follows redirects, so there is no redirect barrier either.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the body copied back to the client by io.Copy at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) registers the handler on the public listener
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil) binds to all interfaces, so the handler is public ingress
target := r.URL.Query().Get("target") reads the attacker-controlled value
http.Get(target) makes the outbound request to the attacker-chosen URL
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the response body, so this is full-read SSRF and not blind

finding.guards_checked: The `allowed` map at main.go:9 is never consulted in fetch(). There is no scheme or host check, no authentication or middleware, no CheckRedirect override (http.Get uses DefaultClient, which follows up to 10 redirects), and no IP or CIDR egress filter in the repo.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the unvalidated `target` query parameter to http.Get and main.go:22 copies the body back, with no guard in fetch(), registered at main.go:41 and served on :8080 at main.go:43; the `allowed` check exists only in the separate safeFetch (main.go:27).
